I am eighty years old now, so carrying heavy bags of chemical fertilizer from the market is too difficult for me, and they cost too much money for my small plot anyway. My family and I will prepare the land together, using the goat manure and compost we have at home to feed the soil, and we will plant the yam setts and cassava cuttings we saved from last season’s harvest. We do not need to buy spray or irrigation because the rains will come as they always do in the South South, and we will pull the weeds by hand when they appear. My children and grandchildren will help me with most of the work, but I will need to hire a few strong young men from the village to help with the heavy mounding at the start of the season.
